title: prefs: add support for bool values to prefs_get_uint_value to fix an ASAN crash, fix wiretap UBSan error
description:
* prefs: add support for bool values to prefs_get_uint_value

    Opening the Endpoints dialog triggers a global-buffer-overflow read
    because it tries to read a 1-byte bool as 4-byte integer when calling
    `prefs_get_uint_value("ip", "conv_agg_flag")`. Instead of extending the
    API surface, let's just extend this function with bool support.

    Fixes: v4.5.0rc0-177-g0a6609f842 ("Qt: IPv4 aggregation summaries for Endpoints dialogs")

* wiretap: don't use void parameter type in wtap_new_ipv6_callback_t

    The wtap_new_ipv6_callback_t was initially introduced to allow
    add_new_ipv6 to be called from the wiretap library. It's first parameter
    is a 128-bit IPv6 address, so let's use that instead of a void pointer.

    This fixes an UBSan error that could cause a crash when CFI is enabled:

        wiretap/wtap.c:1623:4: runtime error: call to function add_ipv6_name through pointer to incorrect function type 'void (*)(const void *, const char *, bool)'

    Link: https://maskray.me/blog/2022-12-18-control-flow-integrity#fsanitizefunction

I can't reproduce the issue with the git master and the default preferences (I'm building on a fresh VM). Are there specific steps to reproduce then I can review seriously ?
Tested, for me it's OK. Please take into account @guyharris 's comment and I will proceed.

> Instead of extending the API surface, let's just extend this function with bool support.

Is the idea here that we want to backport this fix, and we don't want to extend the API surface in 4.4? If so, extending the API surface would probably be the right thing to do in 4.5/5.0.

I was not planning on backporting this. The API is not widely used, there are only two other users in the GUI code for the same `gui.debounce.timer` uint preference.

The current API also has an issue where unknown/invalid preferences are indistinguishable from the zero value. If a new API were to be added for the appropriate types, then I would probably write the result to an out parameter and return `false` on error. Given the few users however, it is not clear if such a conversion is worth it.

> I was not planning on backporting this.

It solves two invalid memory reference cases, so it might be worth backporting.

> there are only two other users in the GUI code for the same `gui.debounce.timer` uint preference.

There are now zero of them - there was already one case where it directly fetched the preference value from the prefs structure, so I made the others do so as well.

Given that the mechanism was designed to keep the preference value in a variable, I don't see a problem with that.

> The current API also has an issue where unknown/invalid preferences are indistinguishable from the zero value. If a new API were to be added for the appropriate types, then I would probably write the result to an out parameter and return `false` on error.

Or we could move the `prefs_get_XXX_value()` routines to epan/pcap.h, with the API being:

1. Call `prefs_find_preference()` to find the preference; if that fails, it's an unknown preference.
2. Otherwise, call the `prefs_get_XXX_value()` with the returned `pref_t *` handle to get the value.

That doesn't expose the internals of a `pref_t`.
